source_title: PaiBox 2.0 Launches Nationwide, Putting Property Repairs and Rehabs on Autopilot - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
Generally available after closed beta, PaiBox's ontology-first platform uses specialized AI agents to run repairs and rehabs on autopilot, from the tenant's first request to the paid invoice, while keeping property operators in control
NEW YORK , Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PaiBox today made PaiBox 2.0, its AI repair operations system, generally available to residential property operators nationwide. PaiBox's AI agents take a maintenance job from the tenant's first message to the paid invoice, handling the vendor calls, quotes, scheduling, no-shows and closeout that property teams have always coordinated by hand. Founder and CEO Sherry Li announced the system's exit from closed beta on the CREtech Innovation Stage last week.
Most AI in property management answers questions and drafts messages. Running the job is harder. A leaking sink is two hours of plumbing and a dozen steps of coordination: photos from the tenant, a plumber who's booked, a second plumber, a quote, an approval, a time that works for the tenant, a no-show, a reschedule, proof the work was done, an invoice, and an entry in the property management system. Real repair jobs routinely run 20 to 30 of those steps, which is where a single general-purpose AI agent struggles. The arithmetic is unforgiving: an agent that gets 97% of individual steps right, chained across 20 steps with nothing checking its work, finishes the whole job correctly only about half the time.
PaiBox uses AI differently, and the reason is where it came from. It started life five years ago as an internal tool for the property team at Sherry Li's own single-family rental fund. To build it, the team took an ontology-first approach, mapping how repair and rehab work actually moves: every status a job can be in, every approval threshold, every handoff, and every way a job goes wrong. The software kept jobs from getting lost, but some steps were too messy for fixed rules, so a person still had to handle them: working out what a tenant actually meant, comparing three quotes written three different ways, or following a group text closely enough to know what everyone agreed to.
Large language models changed that. Those were exactly the steps AI could now take on, and the ontology the team had already built gave AI agents the structure they needed to do them reliably. PaiBox was spun out as a standalone company in 2025 to bring the system to other operators. Today a team of specialized AI agents handles the steps that need judgment, fixed rules handle every step that doesn't, every handoff between agents is checked, and when a job falls outside what the ontology covers, PaiBox stops and asks the operator rather than improvising.
Pilot customers saw 4x team capacity, with the same team able to handle four times the work orders, and the time from work order to invoice fell from 15 days to 5.
"PaiBox has become second nature; it's how I manage daily operations," said Natalie Roberts, Head of Operations, Canyon Residential.
"Everyone is asking whether AI can actually do the work, not just answer questions about it," said Sherry Li, founder and CEO of PaiBox. "It can, but only if somebody does the unglamorous part first. We spent years building an ontology of how property operations really run, and that's what lets the agents finish the job instead of handing it back to a person halfway through."
Operators decide how much PaiBox runs on its own, from fully automatic dispatch to a person approving every quote. Their approval rules and spending limits apply at every step, taking over is one click, and every action each agent took is visible.
PaiBox is built to work alongside an operator's existing systems, not replace them. It works with a wide range of property management systems, taking on the repair coordination that happens outside them and closing each job out back in the system the operator already runs. Jobs go to the operator's internal technicians and preferred vendors first, with nationwide networks of vetted pros where coverage runs out.
PaiBox is an ontology-first AI execution platform that runs repairs, maintenance and rehabs on autopilot for residential property operators. Its specialized AI agents manage the full workflow from initial request to paid invoice, while keeping human operators in control. Learn more at paibox.com.
